messages:
clare: Heads-up — telemetry shows inconsistent client behavior when we route v1 traffic to v2; customers complain about subtle quality regressions and unexpected cost changes. Idea: add a Console 'compatibility dry-run' that runs a simulated evaluation against historical traffic to estimate error delta + token delta without live mirroring. Thoughts?

michael: interesting. Dry-run avoids billing spikes from probes. How do we simulate? replay cached requests to v2 in an isolated sandbox, or replay to v2 but mark as dry-run so it doesn't affect quotas?

tanvi: replaying cached requests sounds safer. We can sample recent request payloads (X days) and run them in a simulator cluster that has CPU-only cheaper capacity or small GPUs. Capture latency, token counts, and quality signals. Important: surface confidence intervals because cached data skews toward recent usage.

clare: exactly. UX sketch: Console adds a "Run compatibility dry-run" button on a route that will:
- select a sampled window of historical requests (user-visible selector: last 24h / 7d / 30d)
- run those requests in a simulator against v2 variant (sandboxed, non-billable)
- produce a report: error-rate delta, median latency delta, projected token delta, and a cost-preview estimate
- include a small sample of mismatched outputs for manual inspection

infra-bot: infra-bot: feature flag created: feature.console.compat_dryrun -> targeting staging and canary cohorts

michael: two infra asks: 1) we need to cap replay volume per-tenant to avoid simulator overload; 2) simulator must not count toward customer billing and must be excluded from autoscaling decisions unless we intentionally use probe_volume metrics. We should emit internal metrics dryrun_simulated_tokens and dryrun_requests for capacity planning only.

tanvi: also: we need to ensure replayed requests don't re-trigger downstream stateful systems (webhooks, logs) — run them with a neutralized context (no callbacks) and tag them as dryrun. Add a privacy scrubber step for PII in historical payloads.

clare: good catches. UI copy draft: "Run compatibility dry-run against v2 to preview latency, error, and cost impact for this route. Dry-run uses sampled historical requests and is non-billable." Tooltip: "Dry-run replays sampled past requests in an isolated simulator; outputs are for estimation only and not used for routing."

cs-bot: cs-bot: please surface a CSV export option for the dry-run cost-preview so CS can send spend-impact reports to customers.

michael: alerting: if dry-run shows error-rate delta >4% OR projected cost increase >15% OR median latency increase >200ms, mark the route as "compat-risk" and surface a recommended action: rollout throttle, stay-on-v1, or schedule a manual migration.

tanvi: also add a cohort rollout helper: when dry-run looks acceptable, console can suggest a phased rollout (1% -> 5% -> 25% -> 100%) with automated checks at each gate. The gates use live sampled probes but those probes are tiny and routed to a non-billable probe bucket.

clare: runbook note: steps to abort dry-run: cancel job, clear simulator queues, and remove temporary dryrun metrics from billing dashboards. Also add rollback: if a gate fails in phased rollout, auto-set traffic back to previous distribution and notify ops + tenant.

michael: implement flags (backend contract):
```
feature.console.compat_dryrun.enabled = boolean
feature.console.compat_dryrun.default_window = "7d"
feature.console.compat_dryrun.sample_rate = 0.02
feature.console.compat_dryrun.simulator_bucket = boolean
feature.console.compat_dryrun.phased_rollout_optin = boolean
```

tanvi: for telemetry, please expose these fields in the per-route dashboard: dryrun_error_delta_pct, dryrun_token_delta_abs, dryrun_cost_delta_usd, dryrun_confidence_interval. That makes it filterable for CS and product.

clare: I'll open a short PR with wireframes, a proposed simulator contract, and canary cohort list. Tagging @michael @tanvi. Also will add an accessibility note: dry-run results must be downloadable and include a short summary sentence for quick consumption.

cs-bot: cs-bot: noted — please include CSV export and a one-click PDF summary template for external reports.

clare: PR incoming in ~30m. Any last asks?
